newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH C.BANK INTERVENING TO SUPPORT CROWN - DEALER.
newsitem.headline: CZECH C.BANK INTERVENING TO SUPPORT CROWN - DEALER.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB), for the second time on Thursday, has entered the market to support the crown after it fell some 1.5 percentage points against its dollar/mark basket parity.
"They are in again," said Petr Korous of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka in Prague.
He added that he was not sure of the volumes the central bank was dealing in.
After holding steady at around -3.5 percent below basket parity following the initial intervention and subsequent central bank moves to tighten market liquidity, the crown fell to -5.06.
Dealers said the fall was due mainly to a large investment house in London flooding the market with crowns.
But the central bank's intervention pulled the crown back up, with it trading at about -3.6 percent at 1145 GMT.

The CNB has been waging a war against investors to keep the crown from crashing since last week when a wave of short-selling pushed the currency to more than five percent below the mid-point of the dollar/mark basket, which the central bank uses to fix the crown's exchange rate daily.
Central bank and government officials to date have adamantly ruled out a devaluation of the currency.
Last Friday the CNB raised the Lombard rate from 14 percent to 50 percent in a move bolster the crown, once regarded as the most stable currency in post-communist central Europe.
The CNB through the course of the week has gradually restricted access to the Lombard facility, the last resort lending facility for banks, squeezing market liquidity and further boosting the crown.
The central bank fixed the crown at 30.629 to the dollar and 18.081 to the mark on Thursday, implying a deviation against basket parity of - 3.00 percent after a fixing of -2.27 percent on Wednesday.
